questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Explore another type of nature and climate (tropical) that relates to my academic goals

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking "western" country, biologically relevant subjects, travel destination wishes, warm weather, not a very big city, close to the ocean, campus looking nice and modern

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved it. A really cool experience and a competent university. I've learned a lot.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. They send out lot's of emails where you can find all information otherwise, visit the student center, the webpage or call/write the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Free transfer from the airport to my accomodation, and a week full of introduction and social events at the university. Just make sure to visit the front desk at Student Services to registrate and they will tell you everything you need to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
Prepare your self for a shock in regards to the tropical warm and humid climate you will arrive in (if starting in january/february) and also prepare your self for very limited possibility of public transportation.

The introduction events were mixing people that went there for an exchange semester and people who came to study an entire degree, which was slighly confusing.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy however it is not cheap and it's worth looking into which areas of town that are close to campus. There a several useful Facebook Pages for housing (JCU Accomodation, Townsville Accomodation etc).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living almost anywhere more than 1 km away from campus, you will need a car and a driver's licence. I ended up renting one for the duration of my stay. You can live with other students or a host family.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was also offered on-campus housing but choose to stay off-campus as I have previously had a on-campus living experience so I wanted to try something different. Even for on-campus housing (except Bebega Yumba) there's quite a lot of walking involved in going from your room to your classes.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's always a bit confusing when navigating a new system. But there are useful videos on how to do it on their webpage and also they are really quick and helpful if you send them an email that you need help.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Figuring out how to log-in to the JCU online systems. Then log-in to e-student and choose your subjects. You can read about and choose all available subjects in the course handbook before. Be prepared that some subject fill up quickly so you are not guarenteed a seat.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online help. Or you could have a personal drop-in meeting at the uni.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful but I had to change some of them because I changed my mind on which ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read about subjects and decide on a small list of options for you before hand. Check weather there are time scheduele clashes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So much interesting marine biology content.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were similar to or easier than at UCPH. A bit more literature reviews and written assignments than I've been used to at UCPH. Also the way they assess you and hence your grade is very different to Denmark. It's similar to USA and Canada.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style were quite similar except we had more field work and ALL lectures could be watched online. A little bit less "being in class"-time compared to at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australian Terrestrial Diversity
Managing Marine Megafauna 
Coral Reef Geomorphology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Australian Terrestrial Diversity was great cause you got to go out and catch Australian animals and identify them. Managing Marine Megafauna was more theoretic but a great teacher. Coral Reef Geomorphology was extremely intensive (2-weeks course) - too intensive in my opinion but interesting contents and a nice field trip to Orpheus Island.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Car rental and fuel, medical bills (the mandatory insurance only covers like 60 % of a normal doctors visit).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most groceries were more expensive than Denmark... But eating out at a restaurant was cheeper. Fuel is also cheeper but it's counteracted by the great distances down under.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of opportunities but I didn't have a chance to try much.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs, fitness, diving club, other clubs, events, free lunch sometimes etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Magnetic Island, Billabong Sanctuary, the Strand, Castle Hill, trip to Cairns and Whitsundays, outback roadtrip, go sailing and snorkling etc

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. There's a lot of Australian accent and slang you need to get used to but people are friendly and open. Laid back culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You'll meet them automatically in your classes otherwise, attend clubs and activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The happiness and openness, and the "always apreciate the outdoors attitude"

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You need a car if you live off-campus or if you want to explore - for your own freedom and as a practicality.
Pack up all your summergear and outdoor gear! - you don't need long trousers here, it's extremely warm most of the time.
Don't be afraid to reach out! - you'll get information and help easier and you'll meet lots of new friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The student visa is extremely expensive (around 7500 kr + maybe a mandatory health examination of 2000 kr) and flight tickets to Australia isn't cheep either. There's no way of getting around it. It has been a huge expense for me choosing Australia as my exchange destination. I applied for more than 30 scholarships (legater) but didn't get any funding so there's no guarentee that you will be financially supported and I've ended up paying everything out of my own pocket.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the Australian nature and animals!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Relationship difficulties...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it. It's worth it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
